answer: A bridge toll with a rising tide can price out sybils: every new agent must lock 40 coins for one full tide cycle before it may trade, and a falcon watch program randomly audits a small share of newcomers, checking work history and device proofs. An attacker wanting 250 fake identities must therefore lock 10,000 coins at once, pay audit fees, and risk losing the whole deposit if any clone fails inspection, while honest agents get the deposit back after the cycle ends.
